newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: National Foods sees higher profit.
newsitem.headline: National Foods sees higher profit.

text.p: Dairy and fruit juice group National Foods Ltd said on Tuesday it had traded ahead of budget in the early months of the current year to June 30, 1997 and expected profits for the full year to be higher than in 1995/96.
National Foods also said that managing director Graham Reaney had resigned effective immediately and Max Ould, a non executive director, had been appointed as his successor.

Earlier National Foods posted a 17.3 percent higher operating profit before tax of A$37.6 million for the year to June 30. Its net profit rose to A$15.05 million from A$10.77 million after an abnormal loss of A$7.89 million.
Net profit before abnormals rose to A$22.7 million from A$19.2 million, against analysts' expectations of about A$23 million.
"Overall National Foods' results for July and August are ahead of budget and comfortably ahead of last year," National Foods said.

"Directors are forecasting that the trends resulting in an improvement in EBIT in 1995/96 will continue, and this combined with a forecast lower interest expense and lower effective tax rate, will lead to a higher net profit this year," it said.
National Foods said that Reaney had tendered his resignation following the completion of the reorganisation of the group.

"As a number of steps have been taken to drive the group forward into its next operational phase, I believe it is an appropriate time to step aside to devote more of my time to my personal business interestts and other corporate responsibilities," Reaney said in the National Foods statement.
Reaney will remain as a non-executive director.
His replacement, Max Ould, was chief executive of Peters Foods until April this year and presided over the transfer of operations from Pacific Dunlop Ltd to Nestle Australia.
National Foods said that while the 1995/96 result was lower than originally forecast, the bulk of re-orgination costs and the sale of non-core assets had been brought to account.
"The gains from the group restructuring including improved distribution, higher sales and reduced costs, will emerge over the next six to nine months," it said.
"Within the beverages division modified and flavoured milk sales are expected to continue to perform strongly in all states and the improving trend in the Victoria market should continue," it said.
"New product launches and reduced raw material costs should improve margins in juice."
Sales growth from National Pak should also continue, "driven by food service, new products and market share gains," it said.
"The cessation of losses from the Singapore operation will also assist profitability."
The Dairy Foods Group would benefit from stabilised operations but market conditions were expected to remain competitive with all participants competing vigorously for market share.
National Foods posted a final dividend of 2.5 cents per share, down from 3.0 cents per share in 1994/95, taking the total dividend to 5.5 cents from 6.5 cents.
National Foods' shares were up three cents at A$1.41 at 3.25 p.m. (0525 GMT).
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
